text:
mike_support: Hey team — AcmeCorp reporting a spike of 502/504s to the hosted API in us-east-1 starting ~09:10 UTC. They pasted a couple traces and say failures affect both chat and standard generation endpoints. Customer: heavy PLG usage. Error pattern looks like gateway-timeouts and upstream reset. X-Request-IDs: rQX-9b2, rQX-9b9

irene_oncall: Thanks, I'm on it. Can you paste the top 3 request IDs and sample edge logs? Also noting if this is limited to a single region or model.

mike_support: Pasted logs from customer (redacted):
```
[09:11:02] edge-proxy us-east-1 - upstream_reset: stream_reset, reason=refused_stream, request_id=rQX-9b2
[09:11:04] nginx us-east-1 - 504 upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out), request_id=rQX-9b9
[09:11:06] envoy us-east-1 - 502 bad gateway from upstream (upstream connect error or disconnect), xreq=rQX-9c1
```

mike_support: They also sent curl repro: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate\" -d '{"model":"gpt-3.5-redwood","input":"hey"}'` -> 502 intermittently.

sam_dev: I'm seeing a cluster-wide uptick in 5xx in the telemetry dashboards around 09:08 UTC in us-east-1. Error budget spike aligns with a config rollout on the edge auth proxy at 09:00 (deploy-bot: 2005009800 -> edge-auth-proxy v2.14.0). Rolling back?

deploy-bot: deployment edge-auth-proxy/us-east-1 v2.14.0 -> SUCCESS at 09:01:12 UTC. Canary passed initially.

jordan_sre: Can we correlate with upstream latency to billing/internal-account-service? Last time we saw guest->account lookup thundering cause h2 pool exhaustion and 504s. Check upstream latencies and connection pool exhaustion.

anna_backend: Looking at internal traces: starting 09:06 we have a huge increase in synchronous account-lookup calls from edge-auth-proxy to account-service. P95 latency for account-service jumped from ~30ms to 700ms due to a cache-miss hot path. Trace sample:
```
trace_id: trc-0045
edge-auth-proxy -> account-service (sync lookup) 680ms
edge-auth-proxy waiting for account-service (no local cache) -> blocked thread -> upstream connection timeout -> upstream reset to client
```

mike_support: Customer says requests with no X-Account-Id header were impacted most (guest users).

irene_oncall: That fits. New auth proxy change introduced a mandatory sync lookup for account tier on all requests where header missing (PR 3872). That makes each guest request hit account-service now. Under burst, account-service fails to keep up -> auth proxy backs up -> envoy/nginx upstream timeouts -> 502/504 to clients.

sam_dev: Reproduced locally with a small script: 200 concurrent requests with no X-Account-Id -> account-service QPS spikes, auth proxy threads block, envoy returns 502/504. Repro steps below:
```
# reproduce
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-3.5-redwood","input":"test"}' \
    https://edge-us-east-1.api.redwood.com/v1/generate &
done
```
Expected: normal responses. Observed: ~15% 502 / 10% 504 within 30s.

jordan_sre: Good reproduction. For immediate mitigation we should: 1) disable the new mandatory sync lookup in edge-auth-proxy or roll it back; 2) enable short local cache on auth proxy for guest account lookups; 3) add circuit breaker to account-service calls so auth proxy fails open for short periods rather than blocking the whole request pipeline.

anna_backend: I can push a rollback of the PR today. Quick patch: short-circuit guest requests to a default tier if account lookup is unavailable. Pushing rollback now.

deploy-bot: rollout start: edge-auth-proxy/us-east-1 rollback -> v2.13.7 (2005009501) initiated at 09:28:40 UTC.

mike_support: Customer reported partial recovery around 09:32. Error rates dropped from 12% -> 1.5% within minutes.

irene_oncall: Confirming metrics: upstream error count in us-east-1 dropped sharply post-rollback. However, some residual 504s for long tail requests while in-flight backlog drains — expected.

sam_dev: Postmortem notes in brief: root cause = v2.14.0 change (PR 3872) introduced blocking synchronous account lookups for requests missing X-Account-Id; account-service experienced cache miss storm under burst traffic causing auth proxy threads to block and envoys to return 502/504.

mike_support: Customer impact summary for AcmeCorp: 09:10–09:32 UTC elevated 502/504s, ~12% of requests. Team actions taken: rollback of edge-auth-proxy to v2.13.7, added temporary host-level caching (TTL 60s) on edge proxy for guest lookups, and deployed short-term circuit breaker to fail-open on account-service timeouts.

anna_backend: Follow-ups:
- PR to reintroduce async account-lookup with local cache and graceful degradation (bugfix branch 3872-fix)
- Add automated load test to catch cache-miss storms during future canaries
- Add alerting rule for account-service P95 latency and auth-proxy blocked threads

jordan_sre: Also recommend increasing envoy upstream timeout on the edge for now from 15s -> 20s? I'm not a fan of masking the problem but may reduce end-user 504s while we harden the path. Open to discussion.

sam_dev: I don't want to increase timeouts globally. We'll add the cache + async lookup + circuit breaker and then re-roll v2.14.0 in staged canaries with a synthetic high-concurrency test.

billing-bot: Billing note: several requests failed before billing attribution; ensure we don't double-bill. Run reconciliation for AcmeCorp for window 09:05–09:40 UTC.

mike_support: Noted — billing team will run reconciliation. I'll reply to customer with summary and ask for any additional traces.

irene_oncall: Action items (owners):
- anna_backend: push bugfix branch and schedule staged canary (ETA: today EOD)
- sam_dev: add load-test to canary pipeline + synthetic high-QPS test (ETA: 48h)
- jordan_sre: add alerting for auth-proxy blocked threads and account-service P95 (ETA: 24h)
- billing-bot / finance: reconciliation for AcmeCorp (ETA: 72h)

mike_support: I'll draft the customer update now: brief incident summary, mitigation actions taken, ETA for rollback patch and next steps.

anna_backend: I've opened PR 3880 (3872-fix) that reverts the blocking behavior and adds a local LRU cache with 60s TTL and fallback-to-default-tier on lookup timeout. PTAL.

deploy-bot: PR 3880 -> merge, CI green, canary plan ready.

mike_support: Thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread open while we monitor the canary and the reconciliation.

jordan_sre: Monitoring note: keep an eye on h2 concurrency and envoy GOAWAYs; if we see connection pool exhaustion again, escalate immediately.

mike_support: Closing update: last client-reported failure observed at 09:33 UTC, post-rollback. We'll reopen if new regressions appear. :white_check_mark:
